newsitem.title: POLAND: SPEED SKATING-NIEMANN, RITSMA WIN SECOND GOLDS.
newsitem.headline: SPEED SKATING-NIEMANN, RITSMA WIN SECOND GOLDS.

text.p: Germany's Gunda Niemann and Rintje Ritsma of the Netherlands skated to their second gold medals on the second day of the world single distance speed skating championships on Saturday.
Niemann won the women's 5,000 metres in seven minutes 19.85 seconds after cruising to a gold in the 3,000 metres on Friday.
The six-times world champion was nearly six seconds clear of silver medallist Carly Zijlstra of the Netherlands and 11 seconds ahead of compatriot Claudia Pechstein.

Ritsma, who won the men's 5,000 metres, picked up his second gold medal of the championships when he clocked 1:53.58 to win the 1,500 metres. He finished 1.6 seconds clear of Adne Sondral of Norway while Canada's Neal Marshall took bronze.
"It's great to win two golds," said Ritsma. "I am especially happy about the 1,500 metres win because I was sharp in the turns and stayed fast throughout the race."
German and Dutch skaters continued to dominate the championships, winning three more golds on Saturday to share 15 of the 21 medals handed out so far.
Asian skaters, however, have dominated over 500 metres.
Manabu Horii of Japan sprinted to gold in the men's event in an aggregate time of 1:13.55, clocking the day's fastest run of 36.47 seconds.
Norwegian Roger Strom finished just 0.03 of a second behind Horii, while world record holder Hiroyasu Shimizu of Japan was third after a slow first leg which left him in sixth place.
China's Xue Ruihong won the women's 500 metres on Friday.
Marianne Timmer of the Netherlands won the women's 1,000 metres in 1:21.31, beating compatriot Sandra Zwolle and Germany's Franziska Schenk.
"I saw Zwolle's time and tried not to think about it. I knew that I could not afford even one mistake," Timmer said.
